thread:
ana: Heads-up — spotted a tail-latency regression on rtx-pool after yesterday's runtime tweak. Seems correlated with kernel crossover when KV free memory is low. Profiling attached in the CI build.
matt: Can you drop the pprof flamegraph link? Is it CPU-bound or memory-thrashing?
ana: quick summary: CPU % didn't spike, but we see a lot of small evictions + batch admission rejects. Prefetch kernel switch happens mid-batch and latency jumps ~2x for those requests.
ryan: Evictions during batch formation = bad. Are batches growing because continuous-batcher waits for token budget to fill? Could be our token_budget target + KV headroom mismatch.
sara: This sounds like the case where the batcher doesn't account for KV-resident size per request. For some long-prefetch requests we have big KV footprints and the headroom estimator is optimistic.
ana: snippet from the profiler (condensed):
```
# top stacks
runtime.batch_form        35%
kernel.select_prefetch    22%
kv.evict_loop             18%
kernel.fallback_path      12%
other                     13%
```
ci-bot: Uploaded artifacts: gs://redwood-ci/5223456789/pprof-flame.svg and /logs/batch-admit.log
matt: Proposed quick mitigation: when free_kv_bytes < 1.2x estimated_batch_kv_need, clamp max_batch_tokens to 60% and force kernel=compact (no prefetch). Also add a small random jitter to admission to avoid synchronized growth.
ryan: I like the clamp idea. We should also add a preflight estimator: sample the first request in a forming-batch, estimate kv_delta (hot keys) and adjust admission for the remaining window. That avoids optimistic full-batch formation.
sara: Agree, but be careful about sampling cost. Do sampling only within a 10ms window and only on heavy-request paths. Implementation sketch:
```
if free_kv_bytes < KV_THRESHOLD:
  sample = peek_kv_delta(first_req)
  est_batch_kv = sample * expected_batch_size
  if est_batch_kv > free_kv_bytes * HEADROOM_MULT:
    reduce_admit(max_tokens *= 0.6)
    prefer_kernel = compact
```
ana: Also saw fallback thrash: kernel falls back from prefetch->compact then later back to prefetch for subsequent batches, causing oscillation. We need hysteresis on kernel choice and a separate eviction_sensitivity score.
matt: Hysteresis: keep kernel preference sticky for 250ms per-GPU when toggled, and update eviction_sensitivity as an EWMA of recent evictions.
ryan: Can we add a simple metric exposed in console: batch_admit_reject_rate and kv_eviction_rate per-pool? That will help us correlate and set thresholds.
sara: I'll add metrics and a short-run dashboard. Also will run a canary with a reduced token_budget multiplier and sticky-kernel. Requesting a canary deploy.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for rtx-pool v2026.03.18-kv-safety-probe
ana: For the follow-up perf test, please include a workload with 30% long-history requests (big KV footprint) and 70% short. We want to see real mixing behavior.
matt: I'll push a patch to admission logic with the clamp + hysteresis + sampling preflight. Will include flags so we can A/B toggle in canary.
ana: Thanks. If canary looks good we'll promote and roll new headroom thresholds account-wide. Also add an automated regression test that simulates small free_kv_bytes and ensures batcher reduces admission instead of OOMing.
ryan: Sounds good. I'll pair on test harness and add a unit for the EWMA sensitivity update.
sara: tagging @matt for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
ana: 👍 I'll post perf numbers after canary completes.
